$about: What the words on a label mean: the labelling terms the WSET Level 2 and Level 3 specifications list, each written from the Wikipedia article named in source (src/terms.py). places lists the terms a region's pages show; the places inside it show them too. only lists terms a place shows on its own page but does not pass down. except lists places a term from above must skip (Champagne's still-wine AOCs have no dosage terms).

aoc.name: AOC / AOP
aoc.def: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

igp.name: IGP
igp.def: Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.

vdf.name: Vin de France
vdf.def: France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.

bx-sup.name: Bordeaux Supérieur
bx-sup.def: A regional appellation for red and sweet white wine from anywhere in Bordeaux, made to stricter rules than plain Bordeaux.

cru-classe-1855.name: Cru Classé (1855)
cru-classe-1855.def: In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.

cru-bourgeois.name: Cru Bourgeois
cru-bourgeois.def: A ranking for Médoc châteaux left out of the 1855 classification. Any Médoc property may apply.

st-emilion-gcc.name: Grand Cru Classé (Saint-Émilion)
st-emilion-gcc.def: Saint-Émilion's own classification, first published in 1955 and revised since. Plain Saint-Émilion Grand Cru is an appellation, not part of this ranking.

graves-cc.name: Cru Classé de Graves
graves-cc.def: Graves classified its red wines in 1953 and added dry whites in 1959. All the classified estates sit in Pessac-Léognan.

bourgogne-tiers.name: Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
bourgogne-tiers.def: Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.

alsace-gc.name: Alsace Grand Cru
alsace-gc.def: One of 51 named grand cru vineyards, each its own appellation. The wine must come from that vineyard, name it on the label and meet stricter rules than plain Alsace AOC.

vt.name: Vendanges Tardives
vt.def: Late harvest. The grapes need at least 244 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 270 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.

sgn.name: Sélection de Grains Nobles
sgn.def: Made from grapes with noble rot. They need at least 276 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 306 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.

bj-nouveau.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
bj-nouveau.def: A wine made within weeks of harvest and released at 12:01 am on the third Thursday of November.

bj-villages.name: Beaujolais-Villages
bj-villages.def: The middle tier, from 38 villages in the north of the region, with the crus, such as Fleurie, above it.

sur-lie.name: Sur lie
sur-lie.def: Muscadet left on its dead yeast cells, the lees, after fermentation. It gains flavor and texture from them.

champagne-nv.name: Non-vintage, Vintage
champagne-nv.def: Most Champagne is non-vintage, a blend of several years for a steady house style. In great years a house may declare a vintage and bottle wine from that harvest alone.

blanc-de-blancs.name: Blanc de Blancs
blanc-de-blancs.def: Made only from white grapes. In Champagne that usually means 100% Chardonnay.

blanc-de-noirs.name: Blanc de Noirs
blanc-de-noirs.def: White wine made only from black grapes. In Champagne, Pinot Noir, Meunier or both.

sparkling-sweetness.name: Extra Brut, Brut, Demi-sec
sparkling-sweetness.def: How sweet a sparkling wine is after dosage: Extra Brut under 6 g of sugar a liter, Brut under 12, Demi-sec 32 to 50. Brut is the most common.

qualitatswein-de.name: Qualitätswein
qualitatswein-de.def: German quality wine from one of the specified regions. It can be dry to sweet.

pradikatswein.name: Prädikatswein
pradikatswein.def: Germany's top tier, graded by how ripe the grapes are at harvest. Unless the label says dry or off-dry, expect some sweetness.

kabinett.name: Kabinett
kabinett.def: Light wine from fully ripe grapes of the main harvest, often semi-sweet with crisp acidity.

spatlese.name: Spätlese
spatlese.def: Late harvest. Often sweeter and fruitier than Kabinett.

auslese.name: Auslese
auslese.def: Select harvest from fully ripe or noble-rotted grapes.

ba.name: Beerenauslese (BA)
ba.def: Overripe berries picked one by one, often with noble rot. Rich, sweet dessert wine.

tba.name: Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA)
tba.def: Overripe berries shriveled on the vine, often with noble rot. Extremely rich and sweet. Trocken here means dried grapes, not a dry wine.

eiswein.name: Eiswein
eiswein.def: Ice wine, from grapes frozen naturally on the vine. The must is at least as sweet as a Beerenauslese.

trocken.name: Trocken, Halbtrocken
trocken.def: Dry and medium dry. Under EU rules a dry wine has no more than 4 g of sugar a liter, or a little more when its acidity is high. Medium dry has more sugar than that.

landwein.name: Landwein
landwein.def: German country wine, below Qualitätswein, which since 2021 no longer has to be dry or medium dry under national rules.

vdp-gg.name: VDP, Grosses Gewächs (GG)
vdp-gg.def: The VDP is an association of about 200 estates with rules stricter than the law. GG is its top dry wine from its best sites.

sekt.name: Sekt
sekt.def: Quality sparkling wine. Most is made in tank, and the best by the traditional method. Plain Sekt may be made from imported wine, but Deutscher Sekt must come from German grapes.

qualitatswein-at.name: Qualitätswein
qualitatswein-at.def: Austrian quality wine from approved grape varieties, tested by the state before sale. Prädikatswein and DAC wines sit within it.

dac.name: DAC
dac.def: Districtus Austriae Controllatus, Austria's rules for regionally typical wines. The wine must show the typical character of its area.

aszu.name: Aszú
aszu.def: Tokaji's famous sweet wine, made by soaking noble-rotted aszú berries in must or wine, with at least 120 g of sugar a liter.

eszencia.name: Eszencia
eszencia.def: The juice that drains on its own from aszú berries, with at least 450 g of sugar a liter and only 1.2 to 8% alcohol.

igt.name: IGT
igt.def: Indicazione Geografica Tipica, Italy's broad regional tier.

doc.name: DOC
doc.def: Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.

docg.name: DOCG
docg.def: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.

doca.name: DOCa / DOQ
doca.def: Denominación de Origen Calificada, a step above DO for regions with a record of consistent quality. Only Rioja and Priorat hold it.

do-es.name: DO
do-es.def: Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.

vdlt.name: Vino de la Tierra
vdlt.def: Spain's regional wine tier, below DO.

vino-de-pago.name: Vino de Pago
vino-de-pago.def: A wine from a pago, a named rural site with its own soil and microclimate. All its grapes must grow there.

fino.name: Fino, Manzanilla
fino.def: The driest and palest sherries, aged under a layer of flor yeast that keeps air away. Manzanilla is the same style aged entirely in Sanlúcar de Barrameda.

amontillado.name: Amontillado
amontillado.def: Aged first under flor, then exposed to air. Darker than a fino, lighter than an oloroso.

oloroso.name: Oloroso
oloroso.def: Fortified to at least 17%, so no flor grows and it ages with air. Darker and richer, and naturally dry.

palo-cortado.name: Palo Cortado
palo-cortado.def: Begins like an amontillado, then turns toward the character of an oloroso once its flor dies.

px.name: Pedro Ximénez (PX)
px.def: Made from dried Pedro Ximénez grapes. Intensely sweet, dark brown or black.

cream.name: Cream, Pale Cream, Medium
cream.def: Sweetened sherries made by blending. Cream sherry usually blends oloroso with Pedro Ximénez.

rioja-crianza.name: Crianza
rioja-crianza.def: In Rioja, a red aged at least two years in barrel and bottle, counted from 1 October of the harvest year.

rioja-reserva.name: Reserva
rioja-reserva.def: In Rioja, a red aged at least 36 months, with at least 12 in oak. Whites and rosés need 24 months, with 6 in oak.

rioja-gran-reserva.name: Gran Reserva
rioja-gran-reserva.def: In Rioja, a red aged at least five years, with at least two in oak and two in bottle.

joven.name: Joven
joven.def: Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.

ripasso.name: Ripasso
ripasso.def: Valpolicella refermented on the skins left over from making Amarone or Recioto. It may also be labeled Superiore.

amarone-recioto.name: Amarone, Recioto
amarone-recioto.def: Valpolicella wines from dried grapes: Amarone is strong and dry, Recioto sweet. Both have been DOCG since 2010.

ruby.name: Ruby, Reserve Ruby
ruby.def: The most common port, kept in tanks to hold its bright red color and full fruit. Reserve Ruby is a premium ruby approved by a tasting panel.

tawny.name: Tawny
tawny.def: Port aged in wooden casks, where slow oxidation turns it golden brown and nutty. Older ones carry an age indication such as 10, 20, 30 or 40 years.

lbv.name: Late Bottled Vintage (LBV)
lbv.def: Port from one year, aged in barrel and bottled four to six years after the vintage. Unfiltered LBVs need decanting.

vintage-port.name: Vintage Port
vintage-port.def: Made only from a declared vintage year, with at most two and a half years in barrel. It is built to age 10 to 40 years or more in bottle.

ava.name: AVA
ava.def: American Viticultural Area. A wine labeled with one must take at least 85% of its grapes from that area.

vqa.name: VQA
vqa.def: Vintners Quality Alliance, the appellation system for Canadian wine from British Columbia and Ontario. It guarantees the wine's origin.

wo.name: Wine of Origin, region, district, ward, estate
wo.def: South Africa's appellation system since 1973, nested from regions down to districts and wards. A ward is roughly a European appellation. An estate wine may come from neighboring farms farmed and made together.

cape-blend.name: Cape Blend
cape-blend.def: A red blend with 30 to 70% Pinotage, set by the industry rather than by law. Since the 2019 vintage Pinotage should be its largest part.

old-vines.name: Old vines, Vieilles vignes
old-vines.def: There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

icewine.name: Icewine
icewine.def: Made from grapes frozen naturally on the vine and picked at 18°F (−8°C) or colder. Canada makes more than any other country, over 90% of it in Ontario.

noble-rot.name: Noble rot
noble-rot.def: Botrytis cinerea, a fungus that shrivels ripe grapes and concentrates their sugar when damp weather gives way to dry. If the wet weather lasts, it turns into harmful grey rot.

gi-au.name: Zone, region, subregion
gi-au.def: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.

classico.name: Classico
classico.def: The original heartland of an Italian wine area. Every bottle of Chianti Classico carries the black rooster on its neck seal.

riserva.name: Riserva
riserva.def: A longer-aged wine. Each DOC or DOCG's own rules decide whether it has a Riserva and how long it must age. Chianti Riserva needs at least two years, counted from 1 January after the harvest.

prosecco-superiore.name: Prosecco Superiore
prosecco-superiore.def: Always spumante, and only from the two DOCG hill areas, Conegliano Valdobbiadene and Asolo. Prosecco is made from Glera.

cava.name: Cava
cava.def: Spanish sparkling wine made by the traditional method, mostly from Macabeo, Parellada and Xarel·lo. Other methods cannot use the name.

asti.name: Asti, Moscato d'Asti
asti.def: Asti is a fully sparkling Moscato Bianco wine that may range from bone dry to sweet. Moscato d'Asti is sweet, only lightly sparkling and lower in alcohol.

cremant.name: Crémant
cremant.def: A white or rosé traditional-method sparkling wine from one of France's crémant appellations, made from hand-picked grapes and aged at least nine months on its lees.

ava-or.name: Oregon AVA
ava-or.def: Oregon is stricter than federal law: a wine named for an AVA needs 95% of its grapes from that AVA, and one named for an AVA wholly in Oregon must use only Oregon grapes.

vc-es.name: Vino de Calidad
vc-es.def: Vino de Calidad con Indicación Geográfica, a Spanish tier above Vino de la Tierra and below DO.
